answer: VDF-gated registration: each identity must burn a sequential VDF chain of T=2^30 steps before its key activates. The walnut of this design is the asymmetry — honest nodes compute once, while a farm of n keys pays n×T serial CPU time, not parallelizable. The vine of Sybil growth is thus throttled: 10k identities demand ~10k core-years. Onyx-hard timing proofs verify each chain, so fakery fails. Cost scales linearly while influence stays flat — that's why it holds.
